notes: Identity verified from title Asymmetrical Body Perception: A Possible Role for Neural Body Representations; authors Sally A. Linkenauger, Jessica K. Witt, Jonathan Z. Bakdash, Jeanine K. Stefanucci and Dennis R. Proffitt; Psychological Science 20(11), 1373–1380 (2009); DOI header 10.1111/j.1467-9280.2009.02447.x. Supplied text contains the full primary article with methods, results, discussion and references, not an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied. Target correspondence unresolved: the description specifies hand length, but the located test compares hand area, computed by multiplying perceived width and length and dividing by actual area. Candidate area comparison: printed partial eta-squared .41 (canonical parse Zp 2), t(13) = 3.03, p_rep = .97. The printed probability is p_rep, not conventional p; no conversion performed. Candidate area analytic sample: 15 recruited right-handed participants - 1 excluded for misunderstanding instructions = 14 participants, based on explicit recruitment and exclusion rather than df. These candidates are not assigned to a length-only test. Other results concern grasping ability, accuracy against 1 and strength correlations; no separate length-only comparison is identified in Experiment 3 results. Unassigned replication and success fields are placeholders.
